rendered.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color Allies deck that performs every bending type each turn to draw cards and eventually transform into [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for a life gain, card draw, and damage burst each upkeep. As a backup, [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] can join [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander for an infinite loop of creature tokens and triggers.
weaknesses: Critical: Removing [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] shuts down the card draw engine and both combo lines that depend on it.
Moderate: The Shrine-based engine has only [[Origin of Metalbending]] to answer an opposing artifact or enchantment wipe.
Moderate: With just two interaction pieces, only one at instant speed, the deck struggles to stop a fast opposing combo before it resolves.

avatar aang // aang, master of elements.name: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements

aang, swift savior // aang and la, ocean.name: Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury

plans.primary: The deck chains waterbending, earthbending, firebending, and airbending effects off [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] to draw cards and flip it into [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for a damage-and-draw upkeep trigger.
backups: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] together with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] in play makes infinite creature tokens and triggers.

[[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] can fill the same role as [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] alongside [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for the same infinite loop.

As a backup, [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] can join [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander for an infinite loop of creature tokens and triggers.

strategy.text: Cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3 to begin drawing off its bending triggers.
Play bending spells like [[Earthbending Lesson]], [[Waterbender's Restoration]], and [[Airbending Lesson]] to trigger card draws.
Complete all four bending types in one turn to transform into [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for a life, draw, and damage burst.
As a backup, assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for infinite tokens.
Alternately, swap in [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] for [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] in that same loop with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]].

keep.text: [[Chromatic Lantern]] fixes colors into early Lesson spells for bending triggers.
[[Uncle Iroh]] cuts Lesson costs, keeping the bending engine moving early.

sendBack.text: Lacking early color fixing stalls every bending-based card draw.
Five lands with no spells to cast crowds out the bending plan.

tips.text: [[Monk Gyatso]] exiles a targeted creature so you recast it cheaply, and [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] turns that recast into a 1/1 Ally token.
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles Ally triggers, so [[Haru, Hidden Talent]]'s earthbend trigger fires twice whenever an Ally enters.
[[Jeong Jeong, the Deserter]]'s exhaust ability copies your next Lesson spell, letting [[Water Whip]] bounce and draw twice.

keyCards.card: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
keyCards.job: Draws cards per bending type and flips for a damage burst.
Creates tokens from recast exiled spells and anchors the combo.
Exiles a permanent on entry, enabling the infinite loop.

keyCards.card: Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury
keyCards.job: Alternate combo piece pairing with Appa and the commander.
Grants firebending to countered creatures for extra mana.
Reduces Lesson spell costs to chain bending triggers.
Draws cards and grows whenever opponents search libraries.

assessment.line: The Shrine-based engine has only [[Origin of Metalbending]] to answer an opposing artifact or enchantment wipe.
With just two interaction pieces, only one at instant speed, the deck struggles to stop a fast opposing combo before it resolves.
Removing [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] shuts down the card draw engine and both combo lines that depend on it.
The deck has no fog or pillowfort effect, leaving its slow bending setup exposed to fast aggressive attacks.
Removing [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] before its enter-the-battlefield trigger resolves breaks the infinite loop with [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]].
Despite a five-color identity, the deck has no black sources at all, leaving it unable to cast anything requiring black mana.

rendered.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifacts deck that proliferates counters whenever it taps, growing charge counters on engines like [[Lux Cannon]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]]. Artifact ramp such as [[Relic of Legends]] gets it out around turn 3. Backups include infinite mana from [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]], infinite looting from [[Pemmin's Aura]] and [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]], and infinite turns from [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and [[Magistrate's Scepter]].

strategy: Cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3 and tap it in combat to proliferate counters across your artifacts.
Grow charge counters on payoffs like [[Lux Cannon]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] through repeated proliferate triggers.
Double every proliferate with [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] to speed removal, extra mana, and card draw.
As a backup, assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana.
As an alternate win, combine [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns.

keep: [[Relic of Legends]] ramps toward an early [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] cast.
[[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] turns blue creatures into looters once it lands.
sendBack: Too many lands without artifacts to cast stalls the proliferate engine.
Missing blue or red sources leaves key spells uncastable this game.

tips.text: Attacking with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] triggers [[Tome of Legends]] to add a page counter, building toward card draw.
[[Pemmin's Aura]] repeatedly untaps the creature it enchants, looping [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]]'s tap-draw-discard trigger.
[[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] cuts [[Basalt Monolith]]'s untap cost down, letting it churn out mana again and again.
[[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] can drop charge counters on [[Magistrate's Scepter]] each combat, pushing it toward extra turns.

weaknesses: Critical: The deck leans on a wide artifact board, so a wipe like [[Vandalblast]] can strip most of its engine at once.
Moderate: Losing [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] stops its direct proliferate trigger and the infinite-turn line with [[Magistrate's Scepter]].
Moderate: [[Pemmin's Aura]] enables several of the deck's combos, and removing it at the key window breaks them all.

plans.primary: The deck casts [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and taps it to proliferate counters whenever it becomes tapped, snowballing charge and +1/+1 counters across its artifacts for value and damage.
backups: It can assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana.
It can combine [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns and a lock.
It can pair [[Pemmin's Aura]] or [[Freed from the Real]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] for infinite looting.

rendered.overview: This Colorless deck floods the board with mana rocks and lands to reach seven or more mana, casts [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5, and then slams costly colorless spells that cascade twice off its ability, chaining into removal, wipes and Eldrazi value creatures. A late backup infinite mana loop through [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] can close games once assembled.

strategy: Ramp through artifacts and lands to accelerate toward seven mana ahead of schedule.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5 to enable cascade on big colorless spells.
Deploy mana value seven or greater colorless spells like [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] to chain double cascades.
Use wipes such as [[All Is Dust]] and [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] to clear colored permanents while your colorless board survives.
As a backup, assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana to fuel activated abilities.

keep: [[Basalt Monolith]] in an opening hand signals an early ramp foundation.
Early ramp backed by a way to draw more cards.
sendBack: A hand with no path to seven mana stalls before [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] lands.
Too many lands with no colorless threats wastes early turns.

tips.text: [[Thought-Knot Seer]] strips a card on entry, and casting it at mana value seven or more off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] can cascade into another threat.
[[Darksteel Monolith]] lets you cast a colorless spell for free once a turn, stacking with [[Basalt Monolith]] ramp to jump ahead.
[[Forsaken Monument]] doubles colorless mana from taps, making [[Thran Dynamo]] produce far more mana than printed.
[[Spine of Ish Sah]] destroys a permanent on entry and returns to hand when it dies, pairing with sacrifice effects like [[Metalwork Colossus]].

keyCards.job: Grants cascade twice to big colorless spells.
Refills hand and counters spells via discard.
Produces mana and combos for an infinite loop.
Doubles colorless mana and pumps colorless creatures.
Clears colored permanents while sparing colorless board.
Forces opponents to sacrifice all colored permanents.
Strips a card from an opponent's hand on entry.
Destroys a permanent and recurs itself to hand.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck leans on artifacts for ramp and the combo, so something like [[Vandalblast]] would gut it, and it has no answer in-deck.
Moderate: Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed, leaving [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] as a slow answer to fast threats.
Moderate: Without [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] on board the deck loses its cascade engine and just plays big colorless spells straight.

plans.primary: Ramp hard into colorless spells, then cast big-mana-value threats off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] to trigger double cascade.
backups: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana at no mana cost.

rendered.overview: This Naya deck ramps toward [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7, then swings to reveal cards off the top and drop free Dinosaurs onto the battlefield. Support pieces like [[Forerunner of the Empire]], [[Marauding Raptor]], [[Bellowing Aegisaur]], and [[Polyraptor]] can chain into backup combos that flood the board or pile on counters, while fight and damage effects from cards like [[Zacama, Primal Calamity]] and [[Apex Altisaur]] clear blockers.

keyCards.job: Combat damage puts Dinosaurs onto the battlefield free.
Finds a Dinosaur and damages the board on entry.
Copies itself whenever it takes damage.
Pings entering creatures, feeding the Polyraptor loop.
Spreads counters to every other creature when hurt.
Removes counters to deal damage anywhere.
Casts revealed Dinosaurs for free each upkeep.
Grows a creature then unlocks a free hideaway card.

weaknesses: Moderate: With no instant-speed interaction, a fast combo resolves before this deck can answer it, unlike [[Walking Ballista]] used reactively.
Moderate: Without [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] connecting, the deck loses its main way to put Dinosaurs into play for free.
Moderate: Removing [[Polyraptor]] before it takes damage breaks both of its backup combos with [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Marauding Raptor]].

plans.primary: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] attacks to reveal cards and put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield for free, swarming the board.
backups: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] combine with damage to make infinite tokens and infinite death triggers.
[[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Walking Ballista]] combine to put infinite +1/+1 counters on most creatures.
[[Marauding Raptor]] and [[Polyraptor]] together produce infinite tokens once eight mana is available.

keep.text: A hand with [[Atzocan Seer]] and a path toward [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] is worth keeping.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] alongside a couple of lands sets up the late combo turn.

sendBack.text: Too few sources of all three colors stalls out before Dinosaurs can come down.
A grip heavy on expensive Dinosaurs with no early mana just sits stuck in hand.

[[Descendants' Path]] reveals the top card and casts it free if it shares a type with a creature you control.

[[Boxing Ring]] triggers a fight whenever a creature you control enters, matching it against a same-cost foe.

rendered.overview: This mono red Goblin tribal deck ramps toward [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], then taps him repeatedly to flood the battlefield with 1/1 Goblin tokens. [[Goblin Warchief]] and [[Goblin Chieftain]] grant haste so the swarm attacks the turn it appears, and [[Goblin War Strike]] can end the game by counting the Goblins you control. If [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] joins [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]], the three combine for infinite casts and infinite hasty tokens.

strategy: Ramp out early mana so [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] lands around turn 4 and starts generating Goblins.
Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] each turn to create tokens equal to your Goblin count, growing the army exponentially.
Use [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] to grant haste so the fresh tokens can attack immediately.
Swing with the swarm or close with [[Goblin War Strike]], which deals damage equal to your Goblin count.
As a backup, assemble [[Goblin Warchief]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite casts and tokens.

keep: [[Goblin Matron]] finds another Goblin piece once you can deploy her cheaply.
sendBack: A hand without red sources stalls before [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] ever arrives.
Too many lands with no token makers leaves [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] unsupported.

tips.text: [[Skirk Prospector]] can sacrifice a token from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for mana to recast more Goblins that turn.
Sacrificing a Goblin to [[Goblin Grenade]] triggers [[Pashalik Mons]] for an extra point of damage.
[[Goblin Warchief]] discounts [[Dragon Fodder]], letting you deploy more token makers each turn.

keyCards.job: Taps to multiply your Goblin army each turn.
Grants haste and cost reduction to the Goblin swarm.
Finds another Goblin piece for the engine.
Turns dying Goblins into reach damage.
Converts the Goblin count directly into player damage.

weaknesses: Critical: Repeated removal of [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] strands the deck without its token engine.
Moderate: A resolved [[Cursed Totem]] would shut off [[Krenko, Mob Boss]]'s tap ability entirely.
Moderate: A fog effect like [[Ghostly Prison]] could blunt the combat swing [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] builds toward.

plans.primary: [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] taps to flood the board with Goblin tokens that then swarm for lethal combat damage.
backups: Assembling [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] makes infinite commander casts, infinite hasty tokens, and infinite death triggers.
[[Goblin War Strike]] can close a game outright once enough Goblins are on the battlefield.

rendered.overview: [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] lead a Jeskai Gods deck built around experience counters. Attacking with Gods or having one die earns counters that [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] dumps onto a creature as +1/+1 counters each end step. Proliferate cards such as [[Inexorable Tide]], [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]], and [[Contentious Plan]] multiply those counters quickly, while [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] converts them into extra cards and direct damage. Extra-combat spells like [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] let the growing attackers swing again for the win.

strategy: Cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]], then attack with Gods to earn experience counters.
Proliferate with [[Inexorable Tide]], [[Contentious Plan]], and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] to multiply those counters.
Each end step, [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] dumps all experience counters onto one creature as +1/+1 counters.
As a backup, cast [[Aggravated Assault]] or [[World at War]] for extra combats with your pumped Gods.
[[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] draws cards for every experience counter and deals 2 damage to each opponent.

keep: [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] into an attack starts the experience-counter engine fast.
[[Contentious Plan]] proliferates counters while refilling your hand early.
sendBack: A hand lacking red or white mana stalls before casting [[Kratos, Stoic Father]].

tips.text: [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles each proliferate triggered by [[Inexorable Tide]], snowballing counters quickly.
[[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] puts a creature onto the battlefield, triggering [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] for damage.
[[Bident of Thassa]] draws cards whenever the Rebel tokens made by [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] deal combat damage.

keyCards.job: Gets experience counters, dumps them as counters.
Draws cards per experience counter, deals damage.
Doubles every proliferate trigger in the deck.
Proliferates experience counters whenever you cast spells.
Proliferates counters, then draws a card.
Deals damage when creatures you control enter.
Attacks for experience, creates attacking Rebel tokens.
Untaps creatures for extra combat phases.

weaknesses: Moderate: Indestructible Gods like [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] fold to exile wipes such as [[Farewell]].
Moderate: Losing [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] stops experience counters from ever becoming stacked +1/+1 counters.
Minor: The deck's main plan is attacking with pumped Gods, so a simple [[Fog]] effect halts a turn's damage.

plans.primary: The deck attacks with its Gods to generate experience counters that [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] turns into stacked +1/+1 counters for combat damage.
backups: Proliferate pieces like [[Inexorable Tide]], [[Contentious Plan]], and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] multiply experience counters faster than combat alone.
[[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] draws extra cards off stored experience counters while pinging each opponent for 2 damage.
Extra combat spells such as [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] let pumped Gods attack again in the same turn.

rendered.overview: A Dimir ninjutsu deck built around [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]]: cheap unblockable creatures like [[Changeling Outcast]] and [[Tormented Soul]] swap into Ninjas each combat, draining life equal to revealed cards' mana values while [[Satoru Umezawa]] and [[Silver-Fur Master]] make the swaps cheaper and bigger. Ninjas like [[Fallen Shinobi]], [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]], and [[Higure, the Still Wind]] add card advantage, reanimation, and tutoring off combat damage. Extra turns and reanimation back up the attack if combat stalls.

strategy: Play cheap evasive creatures like [[Changeling Outcast]] or [[Tormented Soul]] to attack unblocked early.
Ninjutsu [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] in from the command zone off an unblocked attacker to start the drain engine.
Chain ninjutsu into [[Fallen Shinobi]], [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]], and [[Higure, the Still Wind]] for extra value off combat damage.
Use [[Satoru Umezawa]] to grant ninjutsu to the rest of your hand, flooding the board with cheap attackers.
As a backup, [[Reanimate]] can return [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] directly to keep the reanimation plan going.

keep: [[Changeling Outcast]] with early mana sets up ninjutsu into Yuriko right away.
sendBack: A hand with no evasive attacker can't turn on any ninjutsu trigger.

tips.text: [[Silver-Fur Master]] cuts ninjutsu costs and pumps other Ninjas, making [[Fallen Shinobi]] cheaper to sneak in.
[[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]]'s combat damage trigger reanimates a creature, echoing what [[Reanimate]] does from your hand.
[[Satoru Umezawa]] grants ninjutsu to creatures in hand, letting [[Changeling Outcast]] slip in unblocked to enable it.
[[Moon-Circuit Hacker]]'s combat damage trigger draws a card, stacking with [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] for more draws each turn.

keyCards.job: Drains opponents off revealed card's mana value.
Grants hand creatures ninjutsu for cheap attacks.
Lowers ninjutsu costs and pumps other Ninjas.
Always unblocked to enable ninjutsu swaps.
Reanimates a creature when it connects.
Lets you cast cards from an opponent's library.
Puts a creature from any graveyard onto the battlefield.
Tutors a Ninja card after connecting.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck leans on [[Reanimate]] and [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]], so graveyard hate like [[Bojuka Bog]] on their side shuts off that plan.
Moderate: No spell in the deck answers an opposing artifact or enchantment, leaving a pillowfort piece like [[Ghostly Prison]] unanswered.
Moderate: Repeated removal on [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] cuts the life-drain engine even though Ninjas like [[Fallen Shinobi]] still fight on.

plans.primary: The deck ninjutsus evasive attackers into [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] to drain opponents off the mana value of revealed cards every combat.
backups: [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Reanimate]] can put creatures from any graveyard onto the battlefield as a secondary plan.
Extra-turn spells like [[Temporal Manipulation]], [[Time Warp]], and [[Expropriate]] can pile on additional attacks or seize permanents.
